Regular Council Meeting
CITY OF SOLANA BEACH
Regular Council Meeting
Solana Beach City Council, Redevelopment Agency, and Public Financing Authority
MINUTES
JOINT REGULAR MEETING
Wednesday, June 22, 2011
06:00 P.M.
City Hall Council Chambers, 635 S. Highway 101, Solana Beach, California
The City Council acts as the City of Solana Beach Redevelopment Agency and the Public Financing Authority.
CALL TO ORDER AND ROLL CALL:
Present:
Heebner, Kellejian, Roberts, Nichols, and Campbell.
Absent:
None.
Also Present:
David Ott, City Manager
Johanna Canlas, City Attorney
Angela Ivey, City Clerk
Wende Protzman, Dir. Admin. Serv/Deputy City Mgr
Tina Christiansen, Community Dev. Dir.
Mo Sammak, City Engineer/Public Works Dir.
Marie Berkuti, Finance Manager
Mayor Heebner called the meeting to order at 6:06 p.m.
CLOSED SESSION REPORT: (when applicable)
None
FLAG SALUTE:
Mayor Heebner led the flag salute.
APPROVAL OF AGENDA:
MOTION: Moved by Roberts and seconded by Kellejian.
Motion carried unanimously.
PROCLAMATIONS:
1.
City Hall Replanting Certificates of Appreciation
Mayor Heebner presented a proclamation to citizens who beautified City Hall flower beds and scenery.
PRESENTATIONS: None
(Ceremonial items that do not contain in-depth discussion and no action/direction.)
ORAL COMMUNICATIONS:
This portion of the agenda provides an opportunity for members of the public to address the City Council on items relating to City business and not appearing on today's agenda by submitting a speaker slip (located on the back table) to the City Clerk. Comments relating to items on this evening's agenda are taken at the time the items are heard. Pursuant to the Brown Act, no action shall be taken by the City Council on public comment items. Council may refer items to the City Manager for placement on a future agenda. The maximum time allotted for each presentation is THREE MINUTES (SBMC 2.04.190). Please be aware of the timer light on the Council Dais.
None
COMMUNITY ANNOUNCEMENTS:
Council reported community announcements.
COMMENTARY:
Council made commentary.
A.
CONSENT CALENDAR: (Action Items) (A.1.- A.8.)
Items listed on the Consent Calendar are to be acted in a single action of the City Council unless pulled for discussion.
Any member of the public may address the City Council on an item of concern by submitting to the City Clerk a speaker slip
(located on the back table) before the Consent Calendar is addressed.
Those items removed from the Consent Calendar by a member of the Council will be trailed to the end of the agenda,
while Consent Calendar items removed by the public will be discussed immediately after approval of
the Consent Calendar.
A.1.
Waive the reading of Ordinances.
Recommendation: That the City Council
1.
Approve waiving the text reading of ordinances on this agenda pursuant to Solana Beach Municipal Code Section 2.04.460.
MOTION: Moved by Nichols and seconded by Campbell.
Motion carried unanimously.
A.2.
Minutes of the City Council.
Recommendation: That the City Council
1.
Approve the Minutes of the City Council Meetings held February 23, 2011, March 10, 2011 and March 23, 2011.
MOTION: Moved by Nichols and seconded by Campbell.
Motion carried unanimously.
A.3.
Register Of Demands. (File 0300-30)
Recommendation: That the City Council
1.
Ratify the list of demands for May 14 - 27, 2011.
MOTION: Moved by Nichols and seconded by Campbell.
Motion carried unanimously.
A.4.
Monthly Investment Reports. (File 0350-45)
Recommendation: That the City Council
1.
Accept and file the attached Cash and Investment Reports for the month of February.
MOTION: Moved by Nichols and seconded by Campbell.
Motion carried unanimously.
A.5.
Award a 1-year Maintenance Contract for Street Sweeping and authorize an extension of the agreement for up to four additional years. (File 0400-10)
Recommendation: That the City Council
1.
Adopt Resolution 2011-080
a.
Authorizing the City Manager to execute an agreement with CleanStreet for one year; and
b.
Authorizing the City Manager to renew the agreement for the next four years at the City's option. The rate for service in years two through five will increase two percent each year.
MOTION: Moved by Nichols and seconded by Campbell.
Motion carried unanimously.
A.6.
Award a 1-year Maintenance Contract for Streetlight maintenance and authorize an extension of the agreement for up to four additional years. (File 0400-10)
Recommendation: That the City Council
1.
Adopt Resolution 2011- 082
a.
Authorizing the City Manager to execute an agreement with Republic, ITS for Fiscal Year 2011/2012, not to exceed $29,700; and
b.
Authorizing the City Manager to renew the agreement for the next four years at the City's option not to exceed the amount budgeted year. The rate for service for years two through five will increase five percent each year.
MOTION: Moved by Nichols and seconded by Campbell
Motion carried unanimously.
A.7.
Adoption of the Fiscal Year (FY) Municipal Improvements Districts Benefit (MID) Fees. (File 0495-20)
Recommendation: That the City Council
1.
Approve Resolution 2011-087, setting the Benefit Charges for MID No. 9C, Santa Fe Hills at $232.10 per unit for FY 2011-12.
3.
Approve Resolution 2011-089, setting the Benefit Charges for MID No. 9H, San Elijo Hills # 2 at $289.58 per unit for FY 2011-12.
4.
Approve Resolution 2011-090, setting the Benefit Charges for MID No. 33, Highway 101/Railroad Right-of-Way at $3.12 per unit for FY 2011-12.
MOTION: Moved by Nichols and seconded by Campbell.
Motion carried unanimously.
2.
Approve Resolution 2011-088, setting the Benefit Charges for MID No. 9E, Isla Verde at $68.74 per unit for FY 2011-12.
MOTION: Moved by Nichols and seconded by Campbell.
Motion carried 4/0/1
(Recuse:
Roberts.)
A.8.
Adoption of the Fiscal Year 2011/2012 Fire Benefit Fee. (File 0390-30)
Recommendation: That the City Council
1.
Adopt the Resolution 2011-091:
a.
Setting the FY 2011/2012 Fire Benefit Fee at $10.00 per unit, and
b.
Setting the Fee for levying on the tax roll.
MOTION: Moved by Nichols and seconded by Campbell.
Motion carried unanimously.
C.
STAFF REPORTS: (C.1. - C.3)
Submit speaker slips to the City Clerk
C.1.
Prepayment of California Public Employees Retirement System (CalPERS) Side-Fund. (File 0340-95)
Recommendation: That the City Council
1.
Adopt Resolution 2011-101 authorizing payment to CalPERS of $3,132,587 as full payment of the obligation due by the City for its Side Funds by borrowing funds from the Sanitation Fund.
David Ott, City Manager, presented a powerpoint explaining the side fund and the proposal to prepay side funds with a loan from the sanitation fund resuting in significant savings f over $1 million over the next 12 years.
Council and Staff dicsussion ensued regarding that the public should know that PERS (Public Employee Retirement System) required the City to be placed into a pool which carry liabiltiies that all cities within it must pay for, that this was a more prudent way to pay for the liability and reduce the cost, and that it would be a good investment for this fund as well as providing a better return on the investment resulting in growth for the sanitation fund as well as savings of the side fund cost.
Discussion continued regarding the potential for another side fund in the future which would result from Council deciding to enhance benefits, that the fund grew due to a change in the structure of the fund, that the City's policy was now to fund all liability, that the employees making their full contribution would not affect the side fund, that new employees without a side fund create a new baseline, that there were still potential for benefits accrued in the side fund if market rates decline, that normal PERS costs could go up and already had, and that the proposal was to save money and pay away risk on the side fund which raises each year.
Council continued discussion regarding establishing a policy to prevent this accumulation from happening in the future that may include requiring a super majority vote to make the change, that the interst rate was fair while being beneficial to the sanitation fund, and that a policy would not tie their hands but provide for future circumstances.
MOTION: Moved by Roberts and seconded by Kellejian.
Motion carried unanimously.
C.2.
a.Renewing Fiscal Emergency Declaration and Adoption of Fiscal Year 2011/2012 Budget. (0330-30)
Recommendation: That the City Council
1.
Adopt Resolution 2011-098 renewing a fiscal emergency declaration.
David Ott, City Manager, introduced the item and presented a powerpoint (on file) reviewing the budget deficit, that a fiscal emergency was declared in 2009, that since then numeous steps were taken resulting in cutting over $1 million, worked with the business community and proposed a business tax which was defeated in June 2010, that the Fire Management Agreement had resulting in savings of $120,000 annually, that a comprehensive pension reform was completed resulting in significant savings over time, and that employees had not received a cost of living since 2008.
Marie Berkuti, Finance Manager, continued the powerpoint reviewing specific budget adjustments and the current proposed budget.
Council and Staff discussed which projects were designated for in the Capital Improvement Project including storm drain improvement and general plan update.
Council discussed adopting the continuation resolution and have the City Manager return with options for reducing the deficit instead of considering accessing reserves and considering structural service delivery changes.
MOTION: Moved by Roberts and seconded by Campbell to approve Resolution 2011-098
Motion carried unanimously.
2.
Adopt Resolution 2011-099 adopting the Proposed Fiscal Year 2011/2012 Budget and directing the City Manager to return to Council on August 24, 2011, with proposals to reduce the General Fund deficit and amend the budget.
Council and Staff discussion continued regarding the need to cut $500,000 - $700,000, to estalish an Ad Hoc to work with the City Manager on these options, that a few things had be begin on the general plan, that some CIP projects had be done due to legal liability and safety issues, that the final structural deficit was around $400,000, and reviewed the memo from the Buget and Finance Commission with their comments and concerns.
Daniel Powell stated that Del Mar received revenue from parking fees and would suggest that the City consider it.
MOTION: Moved by Roberts and seconded by Campbell to adopt Resolution 2011-100 to return the budget in August for adoption with specific line item options for consideration to reconcile the deficit and bring back a discussion item regarding establishing a Fiscal Sustainability Ad Hoc committee.
Motion carried unanimously.
C.2.
b.Adoption of the Redevelopment Agency (RDA) FY 2011/2012 Budget. (0115-20)
Recommendation: That the City Council
1.
Adopt Resolution RDA 048 approving a budget for Fiscal Year 2011/2012.
MOTION: Moved by Roberts and seconded by Kellejian.
Motion carried unanimously.
C.3.
Council Adoption of Workplan for Fiscal Year 2011/2012. (File 0410-80)
Recommendation: That the City Council
1.
Adopt proposed Fiscal Year 2011/2012 Workplan
Dan King, Sr. Management Analyst, presented a powerpoint (on file).
Council and Staff discussed potential for off-leash dog park and would be added.
MOTION: Moved by Roberts and seconded by Nichols.
Motion carried unanimously.
NOTE: The City Council shall not begin a new agenda item after 10:30 p.m. unless approved by a unanimous vote of all members present. (SBMC 2.04.070)
B.
PUBLIC HEARINGS: (B.1.- B.2.)
This portion of the agenda provides citizens an opportunity to express their views on a specific issue as required by law
after proper noticing by submitting a speaker slip (located on the back table) to the City Clerk .
After considering all of the evidence, including written materials and oral testimony,
the City Council must make a decision supported by findings and the findings must be supported by substantial evidence in the record.
An applicant or designees for a private development/business project, for which the public hearing is being held,
is allotted a total of fifteen minutes to speak, as per SBMC 2.04.210. A portion of the fifteen minutes may be saved to respond to those who speak in opposition.
All other speakers have three minutes each. Please be aware of the timer light on the Council Dais.
B.1.
Solana Beach Coastal Rail Trail Maintenance District Resolutions to Provide For the Annual Levy and Collection of Assessments. (File 0495-20)
Recommendation: That the City Council
1.
Conduct the Public Hearing: Open the public hearing, Report disclosures, Receive public testimony, Close the public hearing.
2.
Adopt Resolution 2011-084 amending and/or approving the Engineer's Report regarding the Coastal Rail Trail Maintenance District.
3.
Adopt Resolution 2011-085, ordering the levy and collection of the annual assessments regarding the Coastal Rail Trail Maintenance District for FY 2011/2012.
David Ott, City Manager, introduced the item.
Mayor opened public hearing
Council and Staff discussed the fact that the adoption of the assessment did not include time shares, that to add it would require a public vote.
Daniel Powell asked about the costs for the 3 different zones, and stated that the rail trail suported non-vehicle traffic, that this would be a community treasure to support by paying more, and that it would be ideal to get one tax bill listing all properties owned and assessments included.
David Ott, City Manager, stated that the City did not control county tax assessments.
MOTION: Moved by Roberts and seconded by Nichols to close the public hearing.
Motion carried unanimously.
MOTION: Moved by Roberts and seconded by Kellejian.
Motion carried unanimously.
B.2.
Streetlight Assessment for Fiscal Year 2011/2012 and Adoption of a Resolution renewing the Solana Beach Lighting District and confirming the Engineer’s Report. (File 0497-30)
Recommendation: That the City Council
1.
Conduct the Public Hearing: Open the public hearing, Report disclosures, Receive public testimony, Close the public hearing.
2.
Adopt Resolution 2011-086 confirming the diagram and assessment; providing for the levy of the annual assessment in a special maintenance district; confirming the Engineer's Report; and ordering the transmission of charges to the County Auditor for collection.
David Ott, City Manager, introduced the item and state that no protests were received by the City.
Mayor Heebner opened the public hearing.
MOTION: Moved by Kellejian and seconded by Campbell to close the public hearing.
Motion carried unanimously.
MOTION: Moved by Kellejian and seconded by Campbell.
Motion carried unanimously.
